Path: write metadata — building an app's interface in Studio | 缺项 | P2

## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`. Filed as ②, but an accepted ADR answers it: the Interface pillar holds app · page · view · form · dashboard · report (ADR-0084). This card is step 1, every nav item type; the create flows are objectstack-ai/objectui#11823

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-07T17:59Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (the nav editor's *Add nav item*) and `navSurface.ts` ⇒ `domain:ui`; rationale: Studio's Interface pillar in objectui. Read on objectui `main` `9990f9e122` and objectstack `main` `aa71c4d9d1`.

- **Why not the decision box:**
  - ADR-0084 (Accepted) names the Interface pillar's types as app · page · view · form · dashboard · report (objectstack `docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md:46`).
  - The builder design's rail is the app's nav tree, "groups + typed leaves: page / object / dashboard / report / view" (`docs/design/builder-ui.md` §6).
  - So completing the pillar is in scope by that ruling; only the order is triage's.
  - Prior rulings read: interface pillar,dashboard,report,page,nav item → 28 hits; ADR-0005 Decision §3, ADR-0005 Decision §6, ADR-0005 Decision §7, ADR-0021 D2, ADR-0021 D3, ADR-0033 Decision §9, ADR-0035 Decision §2, ADR-0035 Decision §4, ADR-0035 Decision §6; plus ADR-0084, read for this grade.
- **Why p2:** in a writable package, the pillar can only build a nav of object lists (measured).
- **Order:** nav item types first. That makes every existing surface reachable with the least code. The create flows (list view → dashboard and report → page) follow on objectstack-ai/objectui#11823, `pm:blocked` on this card.
- **Direction (this card):** *Add nav item* offers every type `NavigationItemSchema` declares: object, page, dashboard, report, URL, group and separator (objectstack `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`). Each picks its target from the package's items.
- **Serial:** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (5,547 lines) is also edited by objectstack-ai/objectui#11791, objectstack-ai/objectui#11794 and objectstack-ai/objectui#11795. Claim after the in-flight one lands, or declare the overlap.
- `Clause-②: no`. Patch changeset in objectui.

⛔ Not on it:

- **Other cards' scope:**
  - the create flows for dashboards, reports, pages and views, which are objectui#11823 (`pm:blocked` on this card);
  - the rail's separator rendering, objectui#11791;
  - the More menu and Advanced trigger, objectui#11794;
  - the narrow-width layout, objectui#11795.
- `packages/i18n/**`.

Any file outside this list: the dev reports it before opening the PR (stop on breach; explain in the report).
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` over these paths: no path-derived mandate; default tier)
Clause-②: no
Responsibility: `objectui app-shell Studio: the nav editor's Add nav item can only link an object, so a writable package cannot put a page, dashboard, report, URL, group or separator into its app nav from Studio | the platform path is right: NavigationItemSchema declares every one of those types, and the runtime console renders them | every author building an app's navigation in a writable package; measured by the filer (Add nav item offers only Link to object)`
Thread-read: 6043752848
Serial constraints cleared: `none` blocking.
- **Triage's serial note:** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is also on objectui#11791, #11794 and #11795. All three are still `pm:queue`, so none is in flight. Fold-or-serial: **serial**, none folded; each is a different defect shape.
- **`area:studio` in flight:**
  - seat 3's objectui#11785 (refusal text, no PR yet). It shares `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` only in its error strips, which this surface leaves alone. Both add `i18n.ts` rows under different prefixes; whichever lands second merges `main`.
  - This seat's objectui#11783 (PR objectui#11840) holds none of these files.
- **Open objectui PRs:** objectui#11840, #11841 (`area:records`), #11844 (dependabot), #11600 and #11069. None touches these files. Read 2026-10-08T00:16Z.
- **This seat:** dispatch is parallel, `batch` 3, on the maintainer's word in this session's chat today: 「改为并行派发，batch 3」.
  - In flight with this card: objectui#11783 and objectui#11838 (claimed alongside, `area:workflow`). Their surfaces are disjoint from this one.

Why `Clause-②: no`: this is Studio's editor for types the spec already declares. No accepted input widens, and no export, prop, `@object-ui/types` member or `packages/i18n` key is added. App-shell's `ENGINE_STRINGS` are unexported. If the fix needs a published surface, the dev stops and reports, and the seat re-claims.

## Review: ACCEPT — PR objectui#11846 (head `eecc053`)

  - `nav-target.ts` (+103) and `AppNavCanvas.tsx` (+11/−2, the separator rename guard).
  - 30 `engine.inspector.appNav.*` rows in `i18n.ts`, EN and ZH.
  - Two new pin files, `packageId` added to four existing inspector suites, and one changeset (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

  Nothing touches seat 3's objectui#11785 error strips or `metadataError.ts`. `doNavSave`, `navPayloadOf`, `NAV_TARGET_READS` and the nav banner are unchanged: the diff mentions `navPayloadOf` only in comments.
- **Clause-② re-read on the diff:**
  - The added `export`s (`NAV_ENTRY_TYPES`, `isNavEntryType`, `navTypeAcceptsChildren`, `retypedNavEntry`) are module-level. `index.ts` names none of them, nor `StudioNavItemInspector`.
  - The new required `packageId` prop is on a test-exported component that is not on the package entry. I accept it as module-internal, as with objectui#11783's `ariaLabel`.
  - No `@object-ui/types` member or `packages/i18n` key changes. `no` holds.
- **Rulings held:**
  - **The type list is the spec's:** `NAV_ENTRY_TYPE_TABLE` is a `Record<NavigationItemType, true>`, so it is exhaustive over the spec-derived union at compile time. On `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 it covers object, dashboard, page, url, report, action, component, doc, separator and group. Triage named seven; the order said to offer what the spec declares, and no member is marked non-addable, so ten.
  - **Step 1 only:** no create flows (objectui#11823).
  - **objectui#11776's save rule still applies:** an unbound entry of any target-bearing type is left out of the save and stays on the canvas. That was measured: an unbound `url` was left out of an accepted save.
- **Mechanism checked on the diff:**
  - `retypedNavEntry` keeps `id`, `label`, `icon`, `order`, `badge`, `badgeVariant`, `visible` and the gates, and drops the old type's target. A separator keeps `id`/`order` only, and a group is born with `children: []`.
  - The old path that let a `page` entry keep `pageName` beside a picked object, which the spec refuses with `unrecognized_keys`, is removed (H2, measured).
  - Pickers read this package's published and draft items, leaving out record pages and object-bound actions.
  - The canvas no longer offers inline rename on a separator, whose spec member has no `label`.
- **Declared deviations, accepted:**
  - The type choice sits in the entry's inspector (radios), not in a menu on *Add nav item*. `addItem` is shared with Setup's app editor, and the inspector choice also retypes existing entries.
  - A group is added flat: the Studio canvas does not nest, which is noted as a follow-up.
- **Tests:**
  - **Pins:** 48 rows in two new files, covering the exact type list, retype key-keeping, the per-type pickers, and a spec-valid save per type.
  - **Reverse check:** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` at base turned the type-list rows red in the predicted direction (no `radio`, no `Type` group). The restore was proven by blob hash.

    - the pickers leave out the record page, foreign pages and object-bound actions;
    - one entry of each type was saved, and both saves were accepted;
    - every entry shows in the rail. The separator's empty disabled row is objectui#11791's.
- **Overlap re-read:** since the PR's base `1e1f09e`, `main` (`455c646`) took this seat's objectui#11840. It shares only `i18n.ts`, in different rows. An in-memory `git merge-tree` with `main` is clean.
